entries.notes: Turkish [aˈdʒemoːɫu] (Wikipedia lead IPA): the c is a j sound and the ğ is silent — 'ah-jem-OH-loo'. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'a-SEM-oh-gloo' (ɐsˈɛməɡlˌuː), which is wrong.
uh-KRAY-zee-uh per Collins. The unassisted phonemizer began with a full a vowel.
uh-LAHN duh BOT-un, based on de Botton saying his own name after the interviewer asks at 00:30. The unassisted phonemizer produced uh-LAYN.
Cambridge: /əˈmɪɡ.dəl.ə/ (ə-MIG-də-lə). The unassisted phonemizer produced 'am-ig-DAH-lə' (ˌamɪɡdˈɑːlə) with wrong stress and vowel.
Collins gives British /ˌætəˈwɑːlpə/ and American /ˌɑtəˈwɑlpə/. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'AT-ə-hyoo-al-pə', which is wrong.

Wikipedia gives UK /bʊərˈdjɜː/ and US /bʊərˈd(j)uː/. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'BUR-dee-oo' (bˈɜːdɪˌuː). No full-name alias: an alias whose phonemes cover only the surname would swallow the given name.
BRAN-dice, as the university and Justice Louis Brandeis's name are pronounced. The unassisted phonemizer produced BRAN-days (bɹˈandeɪz).
Spanish /kaxaˈmaɾka/ (Wiktionary), anglicised 'kah-ha-MAR-ka' — the j is an h sound. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'ka-JAH-mah-ka' (kˈadʒɐmˌɑːkə), which is wrong.
The given name uses the vowel in Calvin or cat. The unassisted British phonemizer produced an open back vowel closer to 'Karl'. Case-sensitive matching avoids unrelated lowercase text.

Italian surname: 'ci' before a vowel is the 'ch' sound, so chal-DEE-nee. Documented by pronunciation dictionaries (Forvo, Italian entry) and consistent with the author's own anglicised usage. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'sigh-al-DEE-ni' (sˌaɪəldˈiːnɪ), which is wrong.

English /ˈtʃɔːrɑːn/, Romanian [tʃoˈran]: Romanian 'ci' is the 'ch' sound. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'see-OR-un' (sɪˈɔːɹən). No full-name alias: an alias whose phonemes cover only the surname would swallow the given name.
Standard English /ˈkɒmədəs/ 'KOM-ə-dəs'. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'kə-MOD-əs' (kəmˈɒdəs) with wrong stress.

French [kubɛʁtɛ̃]: the first syllable is 'koo', not 'cow'. Anglicised without the French nasal vowel. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'COW-ber-tin' (kˈaʊbətˌɪn). No full-name alias: an alias whose phonemes cover only the surname would swallow the given name.
day-KART with silent s, per Cambridge Dictionary. The unassisted phonemizer produced dis-KARTS (dɪskˈɑːts).
DOO-hig per the Library of Congress Say How guide. The unassisted British phonemizer produced dyoo-hig (djˈuːhɪɡ).
ih-LENG-kus, with the Greek chi as a hard k, per Merriam-Webster. The unassisted phonemizer produced ih-LEN-chus with a church-ch (ɪlˈɛntʃəs).
Standard English /ˌɛpɪkˈtiːtəs/ 'ep-ik-TEE-təs'. The unassisted phonemizer stressed the first syllable with a short second vowel (ˈɛpɪktˌɛtəs).
fuh-BREEZ, supported by the recorded English pronunciations and phonetic spelling. The unassisted phonemizer produced FEB-rez (fˈɛbɹɛz).
foo-mee-TAH-keh KOH-guh. Hobonichi gives the author's name reading as 古賀史健（こがふみたけ）. The unassisted British phonemizer said FYOO-mi-take.
German surname: hard g's and ts — 'GHEE-guh-rent-ser'. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'JY-jren-zə' (dʒˈaɪdʒɹɛnzə) with English j sounds, which is wrong.
Wiktionary: /ˈɡɪl.ɡə.mɛʃ/. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'GIL-gay-məsh' (ɡˈɪlɡeɪməʃ) with a wrong second vowel.
gwi-DAR-ah, as the author says it in his own talks and podcast introductions. The unassisted phonemizer produced guy-DAR-ah (ɡaɪdˈɑːɹə).
ee-chee-roh kee-SHEE-mee. Gentosha gives the author's own name reading as 岸見一郎（きしみいちろう）. The unassisted British phonemizer produced ik-ee-AIR-oh KISH-i-mee.
The artist's name is universally jay-ZEE, including in British usage. The unassisted en-gb phonemizer produced jay-ZED (dʒˈeɪzˈɛd).
Dutch given name pronounced yohst, documented by Forvo's Dutch entries. The unassisted phonemizer produced 'juiced' (dʒˈuːst). Case-sensitive to avoid touching unrelated words.
KAHN-yay, per the artist's own usage and pronunciation dictionaries. The unassisted phonemizer produced KAN-eye (kˈanaɪ).
KOO-fuh for the Iraqi city, per Random House's pronunciation at Dictionary.com. The unassisted British phonemizer produced KYOO-fuh (kjˈuːfə).
MISH-uh-lin per Cambridge Dictionary. The unassisted phonemizer produced MITCH-i-lin (mˈɪtʃɪlˌɪn).
Wiktionary anglicised: /wɪn/, /nwɪn/; 'noo-YEN' is listed only as a spelling pronunciation, and the unassisted phonemizer produced it (nˈuːjɛn).
Wiktionary: UK /ˈpɜːʒəʊ/, US /ˈpjuːʒoʊ/ (French /pø.ʒo/). The unassisted phonemizer produced 'PYOO-ji-ott' (pjˈuːdʒɪˌɒt), which is wrong.
PLAY-toe per Cambridge Dictionary. The unassisted British phonemizer produced PLAH-toe (plˈɑːtəʊ). Case-sensitive to avoid touching unrelated lowercase text.
PROOST per Cambridge Dictionary. The unassisted phonemizer produced PROWST.

Standard German [ˈʁɪlkə], two syllables with a final schwa. The unassisted phonemizer dropped the schwa entirely (ɹˈɪlk, 'rilk'). No full-name alias: an alias whose phonemes cover only the surname would swallow the given name.
RAW-shark per Cambridge Dictionary. The unassisted phonemizer produced RAW-shatch.
ROH-ling, like rolling without a strongly sounded second l. The unassisted British phonemizer produced ROU-ling with the vowel in 'out'.
Italian surname, approximately SFORT-sa. The unassisted British phonemizer treated the initial letters as the word 'S' plus 'forza' and produced ess-FOR-za, so a dictionary override is required.

English /ˈsloʊtərdaɪk/, German [ˈsloːtɐˌdaɪk]: the Dutch 'dijk' element rhymes with 'dike'. The unassisted phonemizer ended it '-dake' (slˈəʊtədˌeɪk). No full-name alias: an alias whose phonemes cover only the surname would swallow the given name.
German [ˈveːɐ̯tɐ], anglicised 'VAIR-ter' (as in the Werther effect, named for Goethe's novel). The unassisted phonemizer produced an English w and a voiced th (wˈɜːðə), both wrong.
